data.narrative:
General Galactic, a Seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Halen Mattison and Luke Neise, has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparison universe of one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, narrow peer matching within the same stage and valuation tier proved insufficient to support a median-based approach.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable framework here. Using the $10M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $25M. This multiplier reflects observed progression patterns across early-stage climate and energy technology companies, though the single-method constraint limits confidence.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M to $29M, with a median point of $25M. The width of this range ($8M) reflects reliance on a single valuation method and the absence of sufficiently comparable peer data at this stage and scale. Key uncertainties include verification of the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for General Galactic's specific subsector within climate-energy, and the degree to which the sparse Seed-stage peer set constrains precision. Additional diligence on capital efficiency, technical differentiation, and market-size assumptions would be warranted before final pricing.
